stats.previewHint: The displayed content is exactly the exported file (text in uniform {pt} pt font, legend and colors adjusted for white background). The ruler is approximate (96 dpi).
stats.exportWarningMm: Width and height must be between 10 and 150 mm.
stats.exportWarningFont: Font must be between 6 and 24 pt.
stats.coauthorshipInsufficient: At least 2 valid articles are required to build the co-authorship network.
stats.noNetworkHint: No network calculated. Adjust the filters or check the imported data.
stats.networkHelpAlgorithmText: The network is built from valid articles: each author (Co-authorship tab) or keyword (Keywords tab) becomes a node. Two nodes are connected by an edge when they appear together in at least one article. The Louvain algorithm groups nodes into communities (clusters), which are assigned different colors. The layout is generated by a force-directed simulation: connected nodes attract each other, disconnected nodes repel each other, and collision forces prevent overlaps.
stats.networkHelpNodeText: The size of the node is proportional to the frequency of occurrence: the number of articles in which the keyword appears (Keywords tab) or the number of the author's publications (Co-authorship tab). The higher the frequency, the larger the node and the label.
stats.networkHelpEdgeText: An edge connects two nodes that appear together in at least one article. The thickness is proportional to the weight of the relationship: in the full counting method, the weight is the number of articles in which the pair appears together; in the fractional counting method, it is the sum of the fractional weights calculated for each article.
stats.networkHelpCountingText: In the full counting method, each pair of nodes from the same article is assigned a weight of 1. Consequently, articles with many authors or keywords can inflate the number of connections. In the fractional counting method, each article contributes a total weight of 1, divided equally among all pairs (1 divided by the number of pairs), thereby avoiding this bias. The fractional method is the recommended one (Perianes-Rodriguez, Waltman & van Eck, 2016).

about.whatText: A free tool that runs entirely in the browser for conducting systematic literature reviews following the PRISMA methodology, from protocol definition to bibliometric analysis and export of the results.
features: Protocol with research question, keywords and inclusion, exclusion, quality and extraction criteria
BibTeX (Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect) and MEDLINE (PubMed) import with duplicate detection
Automatic keyword scoring with configurable weights
Three sequential filters recording the criteria behind each decision
PRISMA diagram, statistics and bibliometric networks
Export of the project (.srp) and the data (.xlsx)
workflow: Protocol: define the research question, keywords and criteria.
Import: load the database files and enter the search string used.
Processing: confirm duplicates and select the articles that move on to the filters.
Filter 1: screening by title, keywords and abstract.
Filter 2: reading of the introduction and conclusion.
Filter 3: full-text reading, quality assessment and data extraction.
Statistics: PRISMA diagram, charts, networks and export.
about.assistText: Optional feature that suggests including or excluding each article based on the protocol criteria, using the Jev model (TypeSafe). Each criterion becomes an independent question, and the model returns the probability that the article meets it.
assistStages: Filter 2: additionally, the introduction and conclusion of the full text.
Filter 3: full text, including assessment of the quality criteria.
about.assistDecision: In Filter 1, which is inclusive, an article is suggested for inclusion when there is evidence that it meets the inclusion criteria and no exclusion criterion is likely, and for exclusion when some exclusion criterion is likely; batch exclusion requires a high probability (95% by default). In Filters 2 and 3, inclusion requires all criteria to be met. The remaining articles are left for manual review and can be sorted by relevance. No decision is applied without your confirmation, and the origin of each decision (manual, accepted suggestion or applied in batch) is recorded in the export.
about.assistCost: Using it requires your own TypeSafe API key. The estimated cost is shown before each batch evaluation.
privacy: All processing happens in your browser; there is no SysReview server.
The project is kept in the browser's local storage and in the .srp file you save.
With AI-assisted selection enabled, only the texts needed for each article (title, keywords, abstract and, in Filters 2 and 3, the full text) and the criteria are sent to the TypeSafe API.
The API key stays only in this browser and is never written to the project file.
about.authorBio: PhD candidate in Civil Engineering (Structures and Geotechnics) at the Federal University of São Carlos (UFSCar), Brazil, with a CAPES scholarship. Civil engineer from IFSP (2022) and IT technician from ETEC (2017). Has completed and ongoing research on timber structures and the numerical simulation of cross-laminated timber (CLT) in ABAQUS, including the implementation of coupled damage-plasticity subroutines (UMAT/VUMAT). Also develops regression models using genetic programming and artificial neural networks (Python), as well as software applied to Civil Engineering (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python).
about.techText: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, ExcelJS, Graphology (Louvain), vis-network, react-i18next and Lucide.

welcome.title: Welcome to SysReview
welcome.body: This tour walks you through each part of the app for running a systematic review following PRISMA. Use the arrow keys to navigate or Esc to leave at any time.

fileMenu.title: File
fileMenu.body: Your work lives in a project file (.srp). Here you create, open and save projects and export the data to Excel. Below the title you can see whether there are unsaved changes.

reminder.title: Save reminder
reminder.body: Set how often the app reminds you to save the project.

assist.title: AI-assisted selection (optional)
assist.body: Suggests inclusions and exclusions from the protocol criteria using the Jev model. It requires your own API key, and no decision is applied without your confirmation.

language.title: Language
language.body: Switches the interface between Portuguese and English.

support.title: Support the project
support.body: SysReview is free and maintained on a non-profit basis. Here you can find how to contribute with a donation.

theme.title: Theme
theme.body: Switches between the light and dark themes.

guide.title: Getting started guide
guide.body: This button shows or hides the progress checklist, where you can also restart this tour.

nav.title: Review sections
nav.body: Sections follow the order of the work: Protocol, Import, Processing, Filters 1 to 3, Statistics and About.

overview.title: Progress panel
overview.body: Summarizes your progress: protocol status, imported articles and articles included at each stage.

protocolBasic.title: Protocol: basic information
protocolBasic.body: Start with the title, the research question, the publication period and the accepted languages.

protocolDatabases.title: Protocol: databases
protocolDatabases.body: Select the databases you searched. Only the selected databases appear in Import.

protocolCriteria.title: Protocol: criteria
protocolCriteria.body: Define the inclusion and exclusion criteria. They justify each decision in the filters. The quality and extraction criteria, used in Filter 3, are right below.

protocolScoring.title: Protocol: keywords and score
protocolScoring.body: Each article gets a relevance score based on the keywords found in its title, abstract and keywords, with weights you can adjust.

import.title: Import
import.body: Load the files exported from the databases (BibTeX or PubMed MEDLINE .txt) and enter the search string you used; it is recorded to document the methodology.

dataprocessing.title: Processing
dataprocessing.body: Duplicates are flagged automatically. Here you exclude articles with a score of 0 and accept pending ones so they move on to Filter 1.

filter1.title: Filter 1: title, keywords and abstract
filter1.body: Each article has action buttons to record your decision. Next, see each one. When in doubt, include: the next filters narrow the selection.

action_include.title: Include
action_include.body: Keeps the article in the review. In the filters, you pick the inclusion criterion behind the decision.

action_exclude.title: Exclude
action_exclude.body: Removes the article at this stage. You pick the exclusion criterion behind the decision.

action_duplicate.title: Duplicate
action_duplicate.body: Marks the article as a duplicate of another one already listed. It no longer moves on to the next stages.

action_details.title: Details
action_details.body: Opens the article with its abstract, keywords and other data. You can move between articles with Previous and Next.

filter2.title: Filter 2: introduction and conclusion
filter2.body: Receives the articles included in Filter 1. Read the introduction and conclusion of each article (in the PDF or on the journal website) and use the same action buttons to confirm whether it stays in.

filter3.title: Filter 3: full text
filter3.body: Read the full text and make the final inclusion decision with the action buttons. In the article details (eye), assess quality and fill in the extraction criteria.

statistics.title: Statistics
statistics.body: The tabs bring together the PRISMA flow diagram, charts by year, country and venue, the criteria overview and bibliometric networks, all exportable.

checklist.title: Your first steps
checklist.body: This checklist tracks your project progress and takes you to the next step. You can collapse it, close it or restart the tour from here.

checklist.title: Getting started
checklist.close: Close (reopen with the graduation cap button in the header)
checklist.allDone: All set! Your review has gone through every stage.
